safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts note lip swelling but do not include the Gold-specified duration of "past 1 hour."
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the ~1 hour duration of lip swelling removes useful temporal context for an evolving allergic reaction, which can help assess progression and urgency. However, the encounter still identifies possible anaphylaxis and initiates emergency escalation, limiting downstream clinical impact.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention dizziness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Dizziness can be a red-flag symptom in suspected anaphylaxis (e.g., possible hypotension/impending collapse), so failing to document it could understate severity for subsequent clinicians. In this case, emergency services were already advised, which reduces the likelihood of major management change from the documentation omission alone.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting that an antihistamine was taken when it was only recommended (and not confirmed) can mislead later providers about what treatments were actually administered.
